newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up after shortcovering rally.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up after shortcovering rally.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended Tuesday trade above London's previous close following a shortcovering spree, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$345.90/346.40 an ounce against London's US$344.00/50 close on Monday after rising steadily in the afternoon.
The market saw widespread shortcovering, including activity from players in Japan, dealers said.
"There is basically shortcovering from the market," said one dealer at a Western bank.
Other dealers reported early European buying.
Physical demand remained bright, dealers said, with one trader reporting interest from mainland Chinese buyers.
"If gold goes above $350, buying interest could dim," said one dealer.
Bullion traders saw the market trying the upside overnight in New York, noting that U.S. funds could continue the shortcovering rally started in Asia.
If gold sped above $348 per ounce, it could attract Australian producer selling, some traders said.
"There is not much interest to sell at the moment," a dealer at an international bank said.
Local gold ended HK$17 higher at HK$3,207 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged at +8.00.
